chapter: Mingus and the call from Hampton
title: The Montgomery brothers never really a trio
summary: Their playing was always with drums or a horn because Wes and Buddy had too strong a pulse for light trio work.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: What kind of music was the trio playing?

Yeah. The trio? With the brothers? Well, it wasn't exactly just a trio. We had, at that time, it depended on what the job called for. There were a lot of times you might be working with three, four, five, whatever amount of pieces. We weren't just into it as a trio, really into it as a trio. As a matter of fact, we've never really worked as a trio...

...You gotta have a set of drums or...what's what we've always got. The pulse of our playing hasn't been a light trio work. I think Buddy and Wes both are too domineering to be with a pretty little tasty thing with a trio. They had to have that big, that pulse of their playing went beyond that of a trio. So most of our playing was always with a...oh, we've done some things with a quartet. But the horn is always... add the color to the guitar that was always needed to make it more right. The experience of the playing...
